title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on Romans 1: Paul's greeting to those in Rome, his eagerness to preach the Good News, and what the chapter says about those who suppress the truth.

questions.text: How does Paul describe himself in the opening words of the letter?
questions.explanation: The letter opens, "Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God."

answers.text: A servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle
A teacher of the law brought up in Jerusalem among the elders
An elder of the church in Rome
A prophet sent to the twelve tribes

questions.text: What does the text say about God's Son according to the flesh?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:3 says that his Son was born of the offspring of David according to the flesh.

answers.text: He was born of the tribe of Levi
He came from the house of Aaron, of the priests who serve the temple
He was born of the offspring of David
He was born in Rome

questions.text: To whom is this letter addressed?
questions.explanation: The greeting is to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints.

answers.text: To the elders and the saints who are in Jerusalem
To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints
To all the churches throughout the province of Asia
To the Jews scattered among the nations

questions.text: What does Paul thank his God for first?
questions.explanation: Paul thanks his God through Jesus Christ for all of them, because their faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

answers.text: That they have kept the whole law of their fathers
That they have sent him gifts for the needy
That they have built a house of prayer
That their faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world

questions.text: Why does Paul say he longs to see them?
questions.explanation: Paul says he longs to see them so that he may impart to them some spiritual gift, to the end that they may be established.

answers.text: To collect money for the needy among the saints of his own nation
To settle a quarrel that had arisen among the elders of the city
To impart some spiritual gift, so that they may be established
To appoint elders over them in the city

questions.text: To whom does Paul say he is a debtor?
questions.explanation: Paul says he is debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.

answers.text: To Greeks and to foreigners, to the wise and to the foolish
To the prophets and to the apostles before him
Only to his own nation and to no one else
To Caesar and to the governors of the nations

questions.text: Why does Paul say he is not ashamed of the Good News of Christ?
questions.explanation: He is not ashamed of it because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first and also for the Greek.

answers.text: Because it was given to him by the apostles at Jerusalem
Because it has already been proclaimed before kings and governors
Because it fulfills the law of Moses in every point
Because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes

questions.text: What words does Paul quote as written, after saying God's righteousness is revealed from faith to faith?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:17 quotes, "But the righteous shall live by faith."

answers.text: "The just shall judge the nations."
"But the righteous shall live by faith."
"Without faith it is impossible to please God."
"The righteous shall shine as the sun."

questions.text: What does the chapter say has been clearly seen since the creation of the world?
questions.explanation: It says the invisible things of him, his everlasting power and divinity, are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, so that they are without excuse.

answers.text: The coming day of wrath
The names of his prophets
His everlasting power and divinity
The glory of the law

questions.text: What did they trade the glory of the incorruptible God for?
questions.explanation: They traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.

answers.text: The likeness of an image of corruptible man, birds, animals and creeping things
The wisdom of the Greeks and the learning of the foolish
The riches of the nations, the honor that comes from men and the wisdom of this world
The traditions handed down to them by their fathers
